architecture.document.name: document

architecture.integrates.name: integrates

architecture.person.name: person

architecture.publishes.name: publishes
architecture.publishes.description: A component puts a message on a queue.

architecture.queue.name: queue
architecture.queue.description: A component that carries messages from one component to another: a collection, holding the messages waiting as records (`records.of`).

architecture.reads.name: reads

architecture.yaml.patterns.anti-corrupti.name: Anti-corruption layer
architecture.yaml.patterns.anti-corrupti.body: Use when an outside system must be reached without its model leaking into ours.

architecture.yaml.patterns.anti-corrupti.name: Keeps an outside model out of ours. Everything crossing is translated in one place.
Accepts a request already in our model.
Maps the outside model to ours and back.
The only part that speaks the outside protocol.

architecture.yaml.patterns.api-gateway.name: API gateway
architecture.yaml.patterns.api-gateway.body: Use when many clients reach many services and each request should be checked once, at one way in.

architecture.yaml.patterns.api-gateway.1.name: One way in: every request is authenticated, held to its quota, then routed to the service that owns it.

architecture.yaml.patterns.api-gateway.3.name: Checks who is calling before anything else runs.

architecture.yaml.patterns.api-gateway.5.name: Turns away a caller over its quota.

architecture.yaml.patterns.api-gateway.7.name: Sends each request to the service that owns its path.

architecture.yaml.patterns.circuit-break.name: Circuit breaker
architecture.yaml.patterns.circuit-break.body: Use when a remote call can hang or fail, and a failing dependency must not take its callers down with it.

architecture.yaml.patterns.circuit-break.name: Calls pass while the remote answers. After repeated failures the breaker opens and the fallback answers until a trial call succeeds.
Counts failures. Closed, it passes calls; open, it fails fast.
Answers while the breaker is open.

architecture.yaml.patterns.layered-archi.name: Layered architecture
architecture.yaml.patterns.layered-archi.body: Use when one service owns its rules and its store, and every request should meet them in the same order.

architecture.yaml.patterns.layered-archi.name: Requests enter at the API, rules live in one layer, storage is reached only through the repository.
The only way in. It accepts the request and does no work of its own.
The rules live here, and nowhere else in the service.
Reads and writes the store; nothing else touches it.

architecture.yaml.patterns.saga-orchestr.name: Saga orchestrator
architecture.yaml.patterns.saga-orchestr.body: Use when one business action spans several services, each with its own store, and a failed step must undo the ones before it.

architecture.yaml.patterns.saga-orchestr.name: The orchestrator sends each step's command in turn and records where it is. A failed step runs the compensations of the steps before it, newest first.
Where each running saga is, so a restart resumes it.

architecture.yaml.patterns.transactional.name: Transactional outbox
architecture.yaml.patterns.transactional.body: Use when a state change must announce itself, and neither the change nor the announcement may be lost.

architecture.yaml.patterns.transactional.name: A state change and the event announcing it are written in one transaction, so neither is lost.
Writes the state change and the event together.
The events, written beside the state they announce.
Reads the outbox and publishes each event at least once.

diagrams.aggregation.name: aggregation
diagrams.aggregation.description: A whole and the parts it gathers, which live on without it. The hollow diamond is at the whole, the from end.

diagrams.association.name: association
diagrams.association.description: Two definitions that know of each other: each end says how many, in what role, and whether it can be reached.

diagrams.behaviour.name: behaviour
diagrams.behaviour.description: A method of what holds it: its layer is the flow or state machine that does it, its in-interfaces its parameters and its out-interfaces its return.

diagrams.class_diagram.name: class diagram
diagrams.class_diagram.description: A class diagram: the definitions its references stand for, each a class card — fields, then behaviours — joined by what they extend and the relations stored between them.

diagrams.composition.name: composition
diagrams.composition.description: A whole and the parts it owns: the parts go when the whole does. The filled diamond is at the whole, the from end.

diagrams.dependency.name: dependency
diagrams.dependency.description: One relies on another: a change to the supplier may change the client. Dashed, its head at the supplier.

diagrams.er_diagram.name: entity relationship diagram
diagrams.er_diagram.description: An entity relationship diagram: the definitions its references stand for, each a schema card — columns and keys — joined by the relations stored between them, their ends drawn as multiplicities.

diagrams.flow.name: flow
diagrams.flow.description: Something moves from one to the other: data, material, energy or control.

diagrams.message.name: message
diagrams.message.description: One participant asks another to act: a message between two steps.

diagrams.reply.name: reply
diagrams.reply.description: An answer to a message, drawn dashed.

diagrams.sequence_diagram.name: sequence diagram
diagrams.sequence_diagram.description: A grid read as time: the header row names the participants, and each row is a moment. As a block's behaviour, it is one of its methods.

diagrams.swimlane.name: swimlane
diagrams.swimlane.description: A grid read as lanes: the header row names the participants, the header column the phases, and the lines between steps are drawn. As a block's behaviour, it is one of its methods.

yaml.Catalogue.2-docs.1.name: Order service runbook
yaml.Catalogue.2-docs.1.body:
# When orders stop flowing

Check the **relay** first: `kubectl logs deploy/order-relay`. See the [outbox pattern](https://microservices.io/patterns/data/transactional-outbox.html).

- the outbox table is growing
- consumers report no new events

| signal | threshold | page |
|---|---|---|
| outbox rows | 10 000 | yes |
| relay lag | 60 s | no |

yaml.Catalogue.2-docs.2.name: Charge once
yaml.Catalogue.2-docs.2.body: Checkout retries the same request. The order service treats a repeated checkout key as the order it already created, so a retry never charges twice.

yaml.Catalogue.2-docs.3.name: When payment fails
yaml.Catalogue.2-docs.3.body: A declined authorization does not reserve stock. The order stays pending and the customer is told on the storefront. They may try another card.

yaml.Catalogue.2-docs.5.name: Release notes
yaml.Catalogue.2-docs.5.body: v2 of the orders API: the checkout key is required.

yaml.Catalogue.2-docs.6.name: Incident summary
yaml.Catalogue.2-docs.6.body: Checkout was slow for twenty minutes while the card processor timed out. The breaker opened, the fallback queued charges, and every queued charge was taken once the processor came back, so nothing was lost and nothing was charged twice.

yaml.about.1.name: Shop
yaml.about.1.body:
# An online shop, built from catalogue patterns

Each service in **Containers** is a usage of a pattern from the `architecture` package: API gateway, saga orchestrator, transactional outbox, layered architecture, circuit breaker and anti-corruption layer. Open one to see the pattern inside it.

| Folder | What it draws |
|---|---|
| System | context, containers, deployment |
| Data | the records, and orders that answer them |
| Flows | order states, placing and fulfilling an order, payment retry |
| Catalogue | service specs, runbooks and decisions |
